hero_subtitle: Explore how Lancashire County Council spends public money. With a £1.3 billion annual budget covering education, social care, highways and more, LCC is the upper-tier authority serving 1.2 million residents across Lancashire.
publisher_bio: This website was created by Tom Pickup, Reform UK county councillor for Padiham and Burnley West and Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care at Lancashire County Council. He is also parish councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw. Tom builds transparency tools that make public spending data easier to check.
publisher_titles: County Councillor for Padiham and Burnley West
Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care, Lancashire County Council
Parish Councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw
publisher_quote: It's your money. The more people understand where it goes, the better.

doge_context.political_control: Reform UK majority (53 of 84 seats, elected May 2025). Opposition: Progressive Lancashire 11, Conservative 8, Labour 5, Lib Dem 5, Our West Lancs 2.

spend_triangulation.note: Transparency gross = £4.14B across every class in the published corpus. Procurement-paid (discretionary third-party payments) = £2.96B. Non-procurement rows: Care-Act redacted direct payments to individuals (£303.3M), statutory pass-throughs (£668.5M), accrual journal bookings (£141.6M), settlement noise (£595.8K), internal transfers to pension fund / in-house provider / wholly-owned subsidiary (£61.5M) — all excluded from third-party-supplier forensic analyses. Net revenue budget figures (where published) are smaller again because they net capital, grants received, and reserves movements — transparency totals include all of these.

procurement_paid.note: Discretionary third-party supplier payments — the real procurement footprint.

statutory_pass_through.note: DSG to schools, BCF to NHS ICB, PFI unitary charges, DFG to districts, concessionary travel. Authority has no procurement discretion.

accrual_journal.note: Month-end accrual bookings in the finance ledger. Reverse when invoices clear — summing with paid invoices double-counts.

direct_payment_individual.note: Care Act 2014 + UK GDPR redactions — foster carers, SGO recipients, ASC service-user direct-payment holders. Lawfully unnamed.

settlement_noise.note: BACS / EFT settlement micro-journals. Not a supplier.

internal_transfer.note: Council's own pension fund, in-house provider arm, or wholly-owned subsidiary. Money from commissioner to provider within the authority boundary.

key_suppliers.name: NHS Lancashire & South Cumbria ICB
key_suppliers.note: Pooled Better Care Fund (Chorley & South Ribble BCF) + health & social care integration. Large share is a statutory BCF pass-through, not procurement

key_suppliers.name: Lancashire Renewables Ltd
key_suppliers.note: Waste ALC — part PFI unitary charge (LRL/GRLOL PFI, statutory), part operational waste disposal

key_suppliers.name: Lancashire Schools SPC Phase 1 Ltd
key_suppliers.note: BSF Wave 1 PFI unitary charge — statutory pass-through, not discretionary procurement

key_suppliers.name: HCRG Care Services Ltd
key_suppliers.note: Public Health ring-fenced commission for Health Visiting 0-5. Two ledger spellings (HCRG / HCRG formerly Virgin Care Services) merged here

notable_suppliers.name: Guardian Homecare
notable_suppliers.note: Adult social care — 1,692 transactions, real procurement

asc_market_concentration.description: Adult social care is the genuine concentration story. Six suppliers account for £190M of paid ASC procurement: Guardian Homecare, CGL Services, Alternative Futures Group, Brothers of Charity, Dovehaven Care Homes, Ralph Livesey.

doge_findings.possible_duplicates: £41.1M across medium-confidence groups (same supplier/amount/date, different references)
doge_findings.ch_red_flags: £208.9K to suppliers paid during active Companies House compliance breaches
doge_findings.split_payments: £100.3M suspected across instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
doge_findings.year_end_spike: Levelling Up Fund spent 3.8x its monthly average in March — typical UK-FY year-end pattern
doge_findings.benfords_law: 3.1% max digit deviation — within normal range; no practical evidence of fabricated invoices
doge_findings.weak_competition: ~30 contracts with limited competition, largest worth £110.8M (HH/NHH/UMS Electricity)
doge_findings.supplier_concentration: HHI=32 (unconcentrated) — across the real procurement corpus, LCC's supplier market is diffuse. Top 5 procurement suppliers account for ~7% of paid procurement.
doge_findings.noise_footprint: Forensic findings computed on procurement-only (£2.72B). Excluded as non-procurement: 234,915 REDACTED/REDACT rows (Care Act direct payments, £277M), 13,584 R12 accrual journal entries (£140M), 80,156 EFT settlement micro-journals (£0.6M), 2,248 statutory pass-through rows (£638M), 2,067 LCCG internal-transfer rows (£56M). Data window: April 2024 – February 2026 (23 months, complete). See investigations/DEEP_AUDIT_2026-04-18.md.

political_control.tenure_note: Reform took control on 1 May 2025 — 12 months in office. Briefing focus: motions/agenda items/questions to raise at upcoming meetings, with political sensitivity flagged per item.
